study type: Economic evaluation using systematic review and national registry data with decision tree modeling
exposure: Cesarean section on maternal request (elective CS without medical indication)
outcome: Somatic risks for long- and short-term complications (mother and child)
cohort: The study analyzed primiparous and multiparous women in a Swedish context, using national registry data.
finding: Planned vaginal birth leads to lower healthcare costs and somatic health gains compared with elective CS without medical indication over up to 20 years.
mod_finding: Planned vaginal birth results in lower healthcare costs and somatic health gains compared to elective cesarean section on maternal request over up to 20 years.
